title: Apple discloses HALO humanoid control system using two Qwen models
summary: Apple researchers reported on arXiv on Nov. 4 that they built HALO, a three-layer autonomous control system for humanoid robots, and validated it on a Unitree G1 by transferring motions learned in simulation to an unfamiliar real room. The top layer uses Qwen3.6-35B-A3B to orchestrate tasks, the middle layer uses Qwen3.5-2B to generate motions, and the bottom layer is a reinforcement-learning-trained action tracker. The team released code for data generation, model training, and deployment, according to the report, though the item is a secondary social-media relay and does not supply the arXiv identifier.
